note: The UI text the game speaks aloud, as opposed to the letters, numbers and words a child collects. Help narration is deliberately absent — fourteen long slides per language, rarely heard twice, and the least worthwhile thing here to record.
how_it_works: Each translation template is split on its %s placeholders and every literal fragment becomes one clip. The finish recap already speaks these as separate segments — it substitutes the collected letter or number between them — so the fragments are exactly what the child hears, and no code has to change for them to be recorded. Fragments identical across templates are recorded once; SpeechManager resolves a segment by its text.

why_these.app_title: Spoken once on first boot, to confirm the voice is working.
why_these.recap_*: The finish and gotcha screen. The framing is in the UI language while the letters and numbers inside it are in the learning language, and the two are frequently different — which is why the recap plays as a queue of separately resolved segments.
why_these.lang_*: Spoken in the settings screen when the UI or learning language changes, so a parent who cannot read the menu can still hear which language they picked. Every language name is recorded in every pack, because the name of a language is said in the language of the menu, not in the language being named.

not_recorded.ui.help.*: Fourteen slides per language. Long, rarely repeated, and the poorest return on review time. Stays on the device voice.
not_recorded.remote controller goals: The specification describes narrating these; the code does not, and inventing it here would be a feature rather than a recording.
